title: The Kashf al-Mahjub
author: al-hujwiri
attributionNote: The attribution is not disputed in the scholarship this catalogue follows.
description: The oldest surviving Persian treatise on Sufism, written for a questioner who asked what the Sufis mean by their doctrines and practices. Al-Hujwiri answers with the lives of the early teachers, the rules of poverty and companionship, and eleven 'veils' that set out the path from knowledge to audition.
historicalContext: Written at Lahore in the eleventh century by a Sufi who had travelled through Persia, Iraq and Central Asia. Nicholson's 1911 translation, made for the Gibb Memorial Series, is still the standard English text and the source of most later citation.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time: the whole plain-text edition is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1911 translation by Reynold A. Nicholson is public domain in the United States.
